## What makes this review worth an opus

A pure move is a claim about *absence* — that nothing changed — and absence is what review is worst at. The body-diff harness is the instrument that makes the claim checkable, but it was written by the same people whose work it judges, and it was already broken once: pass 2 found it could not run at all on a one-line dispatch target. **Audit the instrument before you trust its output.** A harness that skips a block reports the same clean line as one that verified it.

Then prove it bites, yourself, on a scratch copy — not on the worktree: perturb a moved statement in one of the handler files and confirm the harness names it; delete a dispatch line and confirm `NO-DISPATCH`; restore. Report what each printed.

## Ticket proposals
- **A pure-move harness should account for every line, not a table of named blocks** — suggested P3; created as [[BAD-078]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: BAD-047's movecheck.mjs is the best instrument the repo has for proving a move changed nothing, and more moves are coming — BAD-052, BAD-053 and BAD-054 all landed the same week. But its design has two blind spots that the next split will inherit: it verifies a table of 37 named keys, so anything the table does not name is invisible; and it drops the two gates' trailing 'return { … };' before diffing, which is precisely where the spike's risk 6 lives (loadRoom must hand back the object it mutated, never a copy). A future harness should account for every line of the old file — the complement of what it matched must be empty and named — rather than confirming a list. That is what BADS-047/Snowden did by hand with an orphan-line sweep, and it is the check that would have needed no hand.
  Evidence: Proved by perturbation on a scratch copy, not argued. With the entire 42-line header doc deleted from index.ts AND loadRoom changed to 'collab: { ...collab }' — the exact bug risk 6 names — movecheck printed 'RESULT: clean (37 moved, 0 inline)' and exited 0. Three section-4 rows have no key at all: the header doc (old 22-63), the retired-blanket-gate comment (790-792) and 'return fail(unknown_mode, 400)' (1229). All three are correct in this PR; I diffed them by hand and they are byte-identical. The harness bites hard on what it does cover — a status code changed inside pull.ts printed 'DIFF download-url' with the unified diff, and a deleted dispatch line printed NO-DISPATCH, both exit 1.

## Outcome
Accepted, and the harness audit is why this review was worth running at all. Being told to distrust the instrument, they did something better than reading it: they broke the tree in the exact way risk 6 describes, deleted the header doc as well, and showed movecheck still printed clean and exited 0. That is a measured claim about what the proof does not cover, not an opinion about it, and it turns the whole PR's evidence from 'the harness says clean' into 'the harness says clean about these 37 things, and a human checked the rest'. Snowden's orphan-line sweep accounting for all 1230 old lines is what closed the remaining gap, and proposal 109 correctly identifies that the sweep is the check that should have needed no hand. The golden replay was run honestly under a constraint rather than around it: the classifier refused stopping the shared serve, so both sides were hosted identically under a bare Deno process and the shared stack was never touched — and the one thing the replay cannot reach is named rather than glossed.
